structural_location.rule_history: Adopted effective January 1, 2002; renumbered and amended effective January 1, 2003; amended January 1, 2007 and January 1, 2016

key_provisions.(c) Definitions: Domestic violence per Family Code §§ 6203, 6211; differential domestic violence assessment defined
key_provisions.(d) Duties: Identify/code DV cases, ensure safety of victims/children, prohibit negotiation about violence or ROs, recommend ROs when appropriate, separate sessions upon request
key_provisions.(e) Intake: Detailed screening for ROs, dependency petitions, safety; forms must inform right to separate sessions
key_provisions.(f) Screening: Throughout process; check for POs, review court docs, interview, consult collateral sources (LE, CPS)
key_provisions.(g) Safety: Consult separately, safety planning (housing, workplace, financial, local agencies), maintain confidentiality of addresses
key_provisions.(j) Training: 16 hours advanced DV training in first 12 months; 4 hours annual update; per Rule 5.230

steward_case_relevance_audit.purpose: Map CRC Rule 5.215 against the steward's 16-year custody history. This rule mandates DV protocols that should have governed every Family Court Services encounter where domestic violence was alleged or documented. The audit asks whether DV screening, safety planning, and separate sessions were properly implemented.
steward_case_relevance_audit.audit_filed_by: Claude (assistant) at first-mouth level; steward review required

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Family Court Services must identify and code domestic violence cases. The audit asks: were DV cases in the steward's history properly identified and coded, or were DV allegations treated as mutual conflict rather than coded as DV?
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — misclassification of DV as 'conflict' is a common protocol failure

factor_audits.factor_id: (d) Prohibit negotiation about violence or restraining orders
factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Staff must not permit negotiation about the violence itself or about existing restraining orders. The audit asks: was the steward ever pressured to negotiate or compromise regarding protective orders or violence allegations during mediation?
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — directly relevant to orchestrated counter-filing pattern

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Separate sessions must be offered upon request, and such requests must NOT be treated as evidence of non-cooperation. The audit asks: if the steward requested separate sessions, was the request honored without negative inference?
factor_audits.audit_status: FLAGGED — requires review of mediation session records

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Screening must include consulting collateral sources: law enforcement and child protective services. The audit asks: did Family Court Services consult LE and CPS records, or rely solely on party statements? If collateral consultation occurred, did it reveal the orchestration pattern?
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — collateral source consultation would have revealed the 911 manipulation pattern documented in project_familylaw_orchestration.md

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Staff must maintain confidentiality of addresses and contact information on all FCS documents. The audit asks: was the steward's address kept confidential, or was it disclosed to the opposing party through FCS documents?
factor_audits.audit_status: FLAGGED — relevant to surveillance and SIM swap pattern

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: All FCS staff must complete 16 hours of advanced DV training within first 12 months. The audit asks: were the FCS staff handling the steward's case properly trained per this requirement and Rule 5.230?
